answer: A strong Sybil defence for an AI-agent economy is a stake-bonded registry whose entry price scales with parallel identities, not with actors. Each agent locks a bond and pays a non-refundable fee, receiving one credential bound to that bond. To farm clones, an attacker must fund every copy separately in a scarce token before any can bid, and payouts stay escrowed until graded, so a large sonnet fleet loses money steadily. A jetty-style rate limiter also caps fresh identities per funding history, and bonds of real quartz weight make mass registration expensive.
